changeset-claim-re-read

## ⚠️ 1 pending changeset(s) describe a file this change touches

Their bodies publish **verbatim** into the CHANGELOG at the next release, so this is a request to **re-read them against your diff** — addressed here because you are the one seat that can answer it without re-deriving anything.

⛔ Nothing here blocks, and nothing here is a verdict on your change. This gate exits 0, is not a required context, and judges **name resolution, never meaning**: it asked whether a pending body names a file you touched. "Is this sentence still true?" is the one question it will not answer, and the one you are being asked to answer.

### `.changeset/6661-app-launcher-nav-menu-renderers.md`

- names `en.ts` → `packages/i18n/src/locales/en.ts` — edited by this change

  > Three new strings — the launcher's and the menu's accessible names, and the menu's empty state — are declared under `console.nav` in `en.ts` and its nine sibling packs. An inline `defaultValue` alone is not a fix: it renders English at one call site and leaves the string untranslatable everywhere (objectui#3517).

Read the **paragraph**, not the line: both false halves of the objectui#8617 claim sat in one paragraph, and correcting either alone would have left it asserting the same wrong thing.

If a claim did go false, **correct the body**. That is precedented and prose-only, frontmatter untouched; `check-changeset-overwrite.mjs` will report the correction as its own case 2 ("correcting a declaration on purpose … legitimate"), which is the intended shape — one gate asks for the read, the other records the write.

Not covered, stated so nobody reads this as more: a born-false claim that spells no line address at all (objectui#9495 coordinated one by ORDINAL — "a grep finds that member first" — and deciding that means reading what the sentence means), a claim spelled as a symbol or a package rather than a backticked file name, and a file named ambiguously.

Compared the checked-out tree with `846cec0ef` (merge-base with origin/main): 13 file(s) changed outside `.changeset/`, read against 1803 pending declaration(s) that publish a body (2413 pending in total). · [run](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/actions/runs/36714434799)

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `02282232a57532bc2da7d5255aafad739ada35d4`
Local-runs: none

Inputs read: card #11206 (body and all three comments: the claim `5910146506`, triage's grade `5910674278`, the os-dev report `5911283798`), PR #11210 (body, 14-file list, the net diff against `main` at base `846cec0efe`, +124/-5), the check-runs on the head, and the two spec sides as source — `DroppedFieldsEventSchema` in `packages/spec/src/data/data-engine.zod.ts` at the 17.5.0 tag commit `0f6dcac5e9` (three arms) and at objectstack `main` `1741c5dcb6` (four, the `computed` arm landed by `b2805465`). Nothing built, run or re-run.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **`STRIPPED_LINE` keyed by `DroppedFieldsEvent['reason'] | 'computed'` — RIGHT.** On the pinned side the union is `readonly | readonly_when | primary_key`, so the key type is those three plus the literal; on the `main` side the literal is already a member, so the key type is the same four. A `Record` over a four-member union with a four-row literal is exact in both directions on both sides: the table stays exhaustive, and the NEXT arm upstream adds is a required key the literal lacks (TS2741, the failure the docblock promises), while a retired arm is an excess row (TS2353), exactly as before. The literal is one named future value tied to `b2805465`, not a `string` widening: `_ReasonIsNotString` in batch 6 still refuses `string`, and `lineFor`'s lookup through `Partial<Record<string, …>>` is unchanged. Nothing exported moves: `STRIPPED_LINE` is module-private.
2. **`satisfies` set aside — RIGHT.** The objectui#9880 precedent (`UNDRAWABLE_VIEW_KINDS`) is `satisfies Record<string, …>` with totality supplied by a separate `Extract`-derived table; `satisfies Record` OF the pinned three-member union would still run excess-property checking on a fresh object literal, so the `computed` row is TS2353 against 17.5.0. The dev's measurement matches the type system; the docblock records why, and the shape chosen keeps ONE table rather than adding a second.
3. **Batch-6 pin `Equal<Exclude<DroppedFieldsEvent['reason'], 'computed'>, 'readonly' | 'readonly_when' | 'primary_key'>` — RIGHT, still exact on each side.** Under 17.5.0 the `Exclude` removes nothing and the `Equal` is the old three-arm assertion verbatim; under `main` it removes exactly `computed` and the remainder is the same three. Any fifth arm survives the `Exclude` and makes the `Equal` false; any removed arm makes it false too; `_ReasonIsNotString` is untouched. This is not a loosened "includes": the only member the assertion is indifferent to is `computed` itself, and the tripwire in item 4 owns that one indifference. The comment names the upstream commit and the shape the pin takes once the pin moves.
4. **The tripwire (`reminds the pin bump that carries computed to retire the widening`) — ACCEPTABLE, and consistent with this repository's own pattern.** It asserts `DroppedFieldsEventSchema.shape.reason.options` of the INSTALLED spec does not contain `computed`, so it goes red only in the ordinary `Test` job of the pull request that bumps `@objectstack/spec` past 17.5.0 — the same moment `_ReasonIsTheEnum` fired at rc.6 (objectui#4167), the same mechanism as `gives every reason the pinned spec declares its own wording` (「A pin bump that widens the enum makes this red」) and `droppedFieldsReason.boundary.test.ts`'s `the skew sentinel is not — and must never become — a spec arm`. It cannot redden the `Spec Main Shape Gate`, which is a type-check-only compile (`TURBO_FORCE=true pnpm type-check --continue`, then `report`), so it does not re-create the outage it repairs. Its message tells the bumper both edits: delete `| 'computed'` from `STRIPPED_LINE`'s key type and make `_ReasonIsTheEnum` the four-member union. One nit, not blocking: the message does not say to delete the tripwire itself; its own title and docblock make that self-evident to whoever reads the red.
5. **The render test for `computed` — RIGHT.** The reason is spelled through a `string` binding cast to `DroppedFieldsEvent['reason']`, so the file compiles against both specs; it asserts the key `detail.writeStrippedComputed` was asked for, the sentence begins "Calculated by the server from a formula", is not "Read-only", and is not the skew sentence. It drives `emitWriteWarning` directly, which is the only path the row is reachable by under the pin (item 7).
6. **`detail.writeStrippedComputed` in all ten locale packs — RIGHT, and none says read-only.** ar, de, en, es, fr, ja, ko, pt, ru, zh each gain the key in the same slot (between `writeStrippedPrimaryKey` and `writeStrippedUnknownReason`), in each file's own quote style and punctuation convention (French spaced colon, full-width colon in zh, the 「次の項目は…」 / 「다음 필드는…」 / 「Поля…」 sibling pattern). Read back: every one says the server computes the field by a formula and the value sent was not applied — ar 「يحسبها الخادم بواسطة صيغة … لم تُطبَّق القيمة المُرسَلة」, de 「Wird vom Server per Formel berechnet … der gesendete Wert nicht übernommen」, es 「Lo calcula el servidor mediante una fórmula … el valor enviado no se aplicó」, fr 「Calculé par le serveur à partir d'une formule … la valeur envoyée n'a pas été appliquée」, ja 「サーバーが数式で計算するため、送信した値は反映されませんでした」, ko 「서버가 수식으로 계산하므로 보낸 값이 적용되지 않았습니다」, pt 「Calculado pelo servidor a partir de uma fórmula … o valor enviado não foi aplicado」, ru 「вычисляются сервером по формуле … отправленные значения не применены」, zh 「由服务端按公式计算，提交的值未生效」. No pack uses its read-only phrase (للقراءة فقط / Schreibgeschützt / solo lectura / lecture seule / 読み取り専用 / 읽기 전용 / Somente leitura / только для чтения / 只读). The table's inline `defaultValue` is byte-identical to the `en` value, which is what `check-i18n-call-site-keys` wants.
7. **The runtime note — RIGHT.** `RECOGNIZED_DROP_REASONS` in `data-objectstack` is derived from the installed spec's `DroppedFieldsEventSchema.shape.reason.options`; `asDroppedFieldsNotice` routes any other wire value to `UNRECOGNIZED_DROP_REASON`, which is not a key of `STRIPPED_LINE`, so `lineFor` answers `strippedLineUnknownReason` ("Not applied by the server"). Under 17.5.0 a server `computed` reason therefore reaches the skew arm, as the changeset and the PR say; the new sentence is used from the first pin that declares the arm, with no further objectui change beyond the retirement in item 4. No accept set moves: the adapter's recognised set is still the pin's.
8. **Cause and population — RIGHT.** The gate's four diagnostics (TS2741 three times at `STRIPPED_LINE`, TS2344 at `_ReasonIsTheEnum`) are the two sites the card named, both of which were written to fail at exactly this upstream move; the diff touches nothing else and the gate, its workflow and its script are untouched. Citations in the diff are by symbol and quoted string, never `path:line` (`Line Citation Gate` green).

### ② Semver level

- Changeset `.changeset/11206-computed-strip-wording.md`: `@object-ui/app-shell: patch`, `@object-ui/i18n: patch` — RIGHT. What publishes is one wording row in a module-private table and one locale key in ten packs; the only other released package touched, `@object-ui/data-objectstack`, changes a test file alone. The fixed group carries both anyway; `Changeset Declaration`, `Changeset Bump Policy`, `Changeset Fixed Group Check` and `Changeset Claim Re-read` are all green on the head. Precedent: the `primary_key` wording (objectui#3935, `21e4585`) — the same shape, table row plus locale key in every pack — shipped under `Patch Changes` in 17.6.0.
- Prose: accurate on every point I could check — the upstream commit and its meaning, "all ten locale packs", never "read-only", the dual-compile purpose, and the runtime paragraph (item ①7). No model identifier anywhere in the changeset, PR body, commits or code comments.
- The PR body's declaration `Clause-②: no` — RIGHT, and it matches the claim's line. The card loosens no accept set (the adapter's recognised reasons are still derived from the pin) and enlarges no public surface beyond one user-facing string key, which is copy, not authorable vocabulary. No `(widening)`/`(narrowing)` arm, so no ADR-0087 marker is owed.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev flag: `satisfies` precedent falsified in part — ANSWERED, agreed (①2).
- Dev flag: a tripwire added beyond the named render test, in the same file — ANSWERED, accepted with one non-blocking nit (①4). A test that fails on a future dependency bump is this repository's established way of making a pin bump say what it changed; the message carries the remedy.
- Dev flag: local compiles narrowed to the closure of app-shell, data-objectstack and console (38 turbo tasks), not the whole repository — ANSWERED by the head's own whole-repository gate run, which is the verdict read below; the local reproduction (red on base, green on head against a spec built from `1741c5dcb62d`) is the dev's report and is not re-run here.
- Dev flag: objectstack `main` moved from `93e9e4263c` (the card's reading) to `1741c5dcb6`; the four diagnostics were identical — ANSWERED, no bearing: the gate resolves `main` once per run and names the sha it compiled against.
- Dev flag: commit trailers use the model-free pair from AGENTS.md — ANSWERED, right by objectui AGENTS.md's own commit-message rule.
- `open_questions`: none.
- Out-of-scope finding: the pin bump past 17.5.0 is the carrier that retires the widening, and until then a formula strip from a newer server reads the skew sentence — AGREED, truthful and by design; the tripwire is the reminder, no card needed now.
- Draft state: the PR is a draft with `mergeable_state: blocked`, which is the dispatched-dev terminal shape (a claim on the card, a draft PR and a report); flipping it ready and enqueueing are the dispatching seat's acts after this record, not a defect of the diff.

**Check-runs on the head (their conclusions are the gate verdicts):** `Spec Main Shape Gate` — **success** (workflow run `36714434848`, job `109883768556`, concluded 2026-09-30T12:36:04Z): this head compiles against `@objectstack/spec` built from objectstack `main`, which is the lane p0 the card is. `Type Check` success, `Lint` success, `Build & E2E` success, `Test (dist pins)` success, `Test` shards 2/8 through 8/8 success, `Changeset Declaration` / `Changeset Bump Policy` / `Changeset Fixed Group Check` / `Changeset Claim Re-read` / `Changeset Overwrite Report` success, `Line Citation Gate`, `Control Byte Scan`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard` and every other completed context success — 38 success and 3 skipped (`Test (coverage)`, its matrix shard and `dependabot`, skipped by design on a pull request) of 42. ONE not yet concluded at this reading: `Test (shard 1/8)`, still `in_progress`. No check-run on the head has failed. The dev's local gate reproduction (red on base, green on head against `1741c5dcb62d`) is their report; the run above is the verdict read here.
